Best Practice
Football Club Stores

15 elements Al Hilal should study — selected from mobile HP audits of Man City, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Arsenal, Liverpool, Atlético, AC Milan & Al Nassr
Mobile viewport · 375–780 px Source: Playwright audit · 2026-08-19 Elements: as found · zero editing Stores audited: 7 of 11
Man City — shop.mancity.com Barcelona — store.fcbarcelona.com Real Madrid — shop.realmadrid.com/pl-pl Arsenal — shop.arsenal.com Liverpool — store.liverpoolfc.com Atlético — store.atleticodemadrid.com AC Milan — store.acmilan.com
Social Proof & Trust
Man City · HP Mobile
01 / 14
Trustpilot Widget on Homepage
social proof · third-party validation
Man City shop.mancity.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Concrete number, third-party verified. "Rated Great · 4.2 · 18,638 reviews" is not a brand claim — it's an external score. Buyers trust third-party validation 4× more than self-declared trust strips.
  • Trust built before PDP. The widget lives on the homepage — not only on the product page. Visitors build confidence before they reach a buy decision, reducing hesitation at checkout.
  • International buyer signal. For a fan in Saudi Arabia buying from a UK club shop, 18K+ reviews signal an established global merchant. No reviews = unknown risk.
no reviews widget — zero social proof in the entire store
Real Madrid · HP Mobile
02 / 14
Official Store Trust Badge + USP Chips
trust bar · structured USP signals
Real Madrid shop.realmadrid.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • One strong identity claim, not a list. "Official Real Madrid CF" is a single badge — confident, not diluted by 6 icons. One clear claim outperforms a strip of vague promises.
  • USP chips = scannable in 2 seconds. Delivery · Returns · Authenticity as chips — each one is concrete, specific, and under 5 words. Al Hilal's strip lists "Customer Support" with no condition or number.
  • Positioned as a conversion element. At 3,200 px on the page — still within the consideration zone. Al Hilal buries its trust bar at 6,237 px, past any buying decision point.
generic icons at 6,237 px · no specific numbers or partner logos
Search & Navigation
Arsenal · HP Mobile
03 / 14
Full-Text "SEARCH" Label in Sticky Header
search affordance · header navigation · discoverability
Arsenal shop.arsenal.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Text label doubles affordance vs. icon alone. "SEARCH" in capitals alongside the icon removes ambiguity — especially for first-time international visitors who may not recognize the magnifier convention.
  • Intent-driven entry point. Fan stores serve two shopper types: browsers (scroll → discover) and searchers (intent-first → type player name). Arsenal's header supports both paths equally. Al Hilal has icon only.
  • Saudi market specificity. Arabic RTL shoppers switching to an English store are more likely to spot a labelled SEARCH than a small icon. Language-agnostic affordance matters for international club stores.
search icon-only — no text label for non-native English shoppers
Liverpool · HP Mobile
04 / 14
Dedicated Search Strip Below Header Bar
persistent search · full-width input affordance
Liverpool store.liverpoolfc.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Search as a first-class navigation element. Liverpool dedicates an entire row to the search bar — not an icon tucked in a corner. This signals that the catalogue is large enough to require search, building perceived depth.
  • Full-width strip = finger-tap-sized on mobile. Icon hits are small (<24×24 px) and require precision — a guaranteed friction point on a 375px screen. A full strip eliminates miss-taps entirely.
  • Promotes search over scroll. For international fans who know what player/product they want, search-first beats category browsing. A visible bar converts latent intent into an immediate action.
icon-only search — no visible search strip or label
Player-First Discovery
Real Madrid · HP Mobile
05 / 14
Shop by Player — Bellingham · Mbappé + Full Squad
player navigation · fan-first discovery
Real Madrid shop.realmadrid.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Fan stores sell players, not products. "Bellingham #5" is a more compelling navigation entry than "Men's Kits." Player names remove one step between intent and purchase.
  • Player popularity = implicit social proof. High-demand players signal what's worth buying. The squad carousel lets fans self-segment instantly by player affiliation.
  • Direct monetization of squad awareness. Al Hilal has elite signings (Milinkovic-Savic, Malcom, Mitrovic). A player grid would directly convert name recognition into product discovery. Currently: no player filter exists anywhere in the store.
no player filter or player navigation anywhere in the store
Man City · HP Mobile
06 / 14
Shop By Player — 12-Player Swipeable Carousel
player carousel · horizontal scroll navigation
Man City shop.mancity.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Player faces are the highest-recognition asset. A swipeable carousel of 12 players gives every fan a personal hook within 2 swipes — faster than scrolling a category list.
  • Photo + name + number = emotional shortcut. The shopper stops scrolling because they see their player — not a category label. Fan stores benefit from emotional interruption, not rational browsing.
  • Two navigation paths in parallel. Man City implements both category grid AND player carousel — serving different shopper mindsets. Al Hilal serves only one path. Second path = incremental reach.
single navigation path via category — no player-based discovery
Homepage → Product Visibility
Man City · HP Mobile
07 / 14
"Our Top Picks" — Direct Product Tiles on HP
bestseller carousel · direct HP → PDP path
Man City shop.mancity.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Shortest path from homepage to PDP. Product tile with price visible → single tap → PDP. No category browsing required. Every additional navigation step loses ~20–30% of shoppers.
  • "Our Top Picks" = implicit editorial curation. The framing acts as social proof — these are the popular choices — without a separate review module. The selection signal does the selling.
  • Al Hilal has 0 products on HP. Industry standard requires ≥6 clickable product links on HP. Al Hilal scores 0 — 117 collection links but no product tiles with price and image.
0 clickable product tiles on homepage — 0 of 6 required
Man City · HP Mobile
08 / 14
Category Grid 2×2 — Men / Kids / Women / Goalkeeper
visual category grid · segment selector · photo-first navigation
Man City shop.mancity.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Photo-first navigation scans in <1 second. 2×2 grid gives equal visual weight to all 4 segments. The shopper's eye picks their segment faster than reading a text list or scrolling tall cards.
  • Goalkeeper as a separate tile = depth signal. A dedicated GK tile catches niche buyers who would otherwise miss it — and signals catalogue breadth without text. Al Hilal serves goalkeepers but doesn't surface the segment on HP.
  • 4 segments, less vertical space. Al Hilal uses 3 tall full-width photo cards. Man City's 2×2 grid shows 4 segments in less vertical space, and covers a segment Al Hilal's layout misses.
goalkeeper segment not surfaced in HP navigation
Hero & Visual Impact
Liverpool · HP Mobile
09 / 14
Hero + Inline CTA Pill — "Shop Now" Over Product
hero banner · CTA placement · direct buy path
Liverpool store.liverpoolfc.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • CTA embedded in hero = zero scroll required. "SHOP NOW" pill overlaid on the jersey hero image converts the first visual impression directly into a purchase action — no separate buttons below the fold.
  • High contrast pill on image. White/light pill on photo background catches the eye without covering the product. The jersey remains visible while the CTA is prominent — both goals achieved simultaneously.
  • Seasonal kit merchandising. Liverpool's hero leads with the new 26/27 Away Kit — connecting the current buying window to the hero instantly. Product-first hero outperforms brand-only hero for commerce conversion.
hero has CTA text but low-contrast placement — pill format missing
AC Milan · HP Mobile
10 / 14
Seasonal Collection Hero — "Summer Collection '26"
hero banner · seasonal campaign · editorial positioning
AC Milan store.acmilan.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • "SUMMER COLLECTION '26" = scarcity + seasonality framing. Naming the collection with a year creates a buying window — shoppers understand this is timely inventory, not always-available stock. Seasonal framing outperforms generic "New Arrivals."
  • Black-and-white editorial photography. High-fashion aesthetic elevates brand positioning. The jersey is presented as clothing, not a sports kit — higher perceived value = higher willingness to pay.
  • Kit launch as an event. Campaign framing of "THIRD KIT 2026/27" turns a standard product introduction into an appointment. Al Hilal's hero shows product without campaign context or naming.
hero lacks seasonal collection framing — no named campaign or collection label
Atlético · HP Mobile
11 / 14
Atlético Madrid — Clean Full-Bleed Hero
hero composition · full-bleed · minimal copy
Atlético store.atleticodemadrid.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Single-message hero — no competing elements. Full-bleed image, one headline, one CTA. Nothing distracts from the main visual signal. "Clarity converts" — minimal heroes consistently outperform cluttered ones on mobile.
  • Model-forward imagery = aspiration trigger. The jersey is shown worn — not flat-lay. The shopper sees themselves wearing it, not examining a product page. Lifestyle image in the hero sets conversion stage before any text is read.
  • No popup obstruction. Clean load — no overlays blocking the hero. First impression arrives immediately — critical on mobile where 53% bounce if load takes >3 seconds.
hero partially obscured by text overlays — composition could be simplified
Personalisation & Premium Upsell
Barcelona · HP Mobile
12 / 14
Customize Your Jersey — 6-Step Builder with Progress
kit builder · step-by-step progress · personalisation upsell
Barcelona store.fcbarcelona.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Visible step counter = reduced anxiety. "Step 2 of 6" — the shopper always knows where they are and how long to go. Al Hilal's builder has no step indicator, creating uncertainty about when it ends.
  • Structured flow increases completion. Multi-step flows with progress indicators show higher completion rates than single long scrolls. Shopper commitment builds with each completed step.
  • Same feature, better UX quality. Both stores have kit builders — the differentiator is execution. Barcelona's builder converts the same feature into a structured, guided experience vs. Al Hilal's monolithic scroll.
builder has no step counter · no progress indicator
Al Nassr · PDP Mobile
13 / 14
Al Nassr (Direct Saudi Rival) — Packshot-First PDP
clean product hero · official naming convention · price + size visible above fold
Al Nassr alnassr.com · PDP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Direct Saudi competitor already there. Al Nassr — Al Hilal's closest rival — leads with a full-frame packshot on white, official naming ("OFFICIAL AL NASSR FC 2026/27 HOME JERSEY"), price and size selector immediately below fold. Standard is set locally.
  • Packshot-first hierarchy. White-background product image takes >60% of viewport before any scroll. Lifestyle image as second slide. This is the global e-commerce standard for kit sales — product clarity beats editorial atmosphere at point of purchase.
  • Sponsor integration without distraction. "HUMAIN" sponsor visible on shirt but doesn't dominate naming or layout — product remains the hero.
Al Hilal PDP leads with editorial imagery — packshot buried or absent above fold
Al Nassr · HP Mobile
14 / 15
Al Nassr — TikTok Social Feed Embedded on Store HP
social video integration · content-to-commerce bridge · fan engagement on HP
Al Nassr store-alnassr.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Direct Saudi rival bridges social and commerce. Al Nassr embeds a live TikTok feed (26.1K–184.8K likes per video) directly on the store HP — real engagement counts are visible, not claimed. Fans already following @alnassr on TikTok see familiar content the moment they hit the store.
  • Content-to-purchase in one scroll. The section sits between product carousels — a shopper sees kit videos with the jersey on pitch, then a product tile below. Emotion → product without leaving the page.
  • Real social proof at zero extra cost. UGC-style vertical videos from the club's own TikTok (verified ✓) carry far more credibility than banner copy. "Champions has a new look" + Ronaldo jersey = narrative that sells itself.
Al Hilal store has no social video integration — content and commerce are completely siloed
Real Madrid · HP Mobile
15 / 15
Multi-Row Product Carousels — Jerseys · Training · Lifestyle
product carousels · multi-category HP surface · direct PDP links
Real Madrid shop.realmadrid.com · HP Mobile
Why it's best practice
  • Three distinct product categories in one scroll zone. Jerseys + Training + Lifestyle in separate carousels — each with price and direct PDP link. The HP functions as a mini-catalogue, not just a navigation hub.
  • Swipeable = browsing without commitment. Horizontal product carousels let shoppers explore without losing their vertical scroll position. Reduces the sense of "going somewhere" — just exploring in place.
  • Price visible in carousel tile = pre-qualification. Showing price on the HP product tile means the shopper arrives at PDP already price-aware, reducing checkout abandonment driven by price shock.
0 product carousels on homepage — no price-visible tiles anywhere on HP
